What does the Bible say about baptism?
What does the Bible say about whether salvation can be lost?
What does the Bible say about the Lord's Supper?
What does the Bible say about whether God chooses who will be saved?
What does the Bible say about faith and works?
What does the Bible say about free will?
What does the Bible say about human nature?
What does the Bible say about the Sabbath?
What does the Bible say about speaking in tongues?
What does the Bible say about what is called total depravity?
Baptism as God's act of cleansing and new birth, given to believers and to the children of believers
Baptism as the sign and seal of God's covenant promise, given to believers and to their children
Baptism of those who believe: obedience to Christ's command and a public answer to the gospel
Falling away is possible: the warnings address people who have been saved, and the one who remains in Christ is kept
The perseverance of the saints (the Calvinist, or Reformed, reading): God keeps those he has saved to the end, and the warnings are among the means he uses to keep them
Eternal security: eternal life is given when a person believes and rests on Christ's work and God's faithfulness, so it is not lost
The bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ: his words at the table say what they are
The body and blood of Christ are truly present in, with and under the bread and wine, which remain bread and wine
Christ is truly present to the believer and received by faith through the Holy Spirit: the bread and wine remain, and are the sign and pledge of what they give
A memorial: the bread and the cup remember and proclaim Christ's death, and the Supper is an ordinance that Christ commanded
God's choosing in view of faith: God foreknows who will trust in Christ and chooses them (what is called conditional election)
God's choice before the foundation of the world, resting on his own purpose and not on anything foreseen in the chosen (what is called unconditional election)
God's choosing of a people in Christ: Christ is the Chosen One, Israel and the church are chosen peoples, and individuals share in the choosing by being in him (what is called corporate election)
Faith working through love: salvation is God's gift, and works done in God's grace belong to the life of the one he saves
By faith alone (what is called sola fide): God declares the believer righteous through faith in Christ, and good works follow as faith's fruit
Faith as obedient trust: believing and obeying are one response to God, and holiness of life belongs to the way of salvation
Free choice, helped by grace: the will is wounded and not lost, and a person freely cooperates with God or refuses him
A will that chooses as it wills, and wills as its nature leads (what is called the bondage of the will): God's working changes the will so that it turns to him
Grace that frees every person to respond (what is called prevenient grace): the bound will is freed by God, and the answer is the person's own
Body and soul made in God's image and called to union with him: the fall brought death and left a corrupted or wounded nature
Fallen in Adam: his sin brought condemnation and a corrupted nature on all his descendants (what is called original sin)
One living person: soul, spirit, heart and body are the whole human being seen from different sides, and each person answers for his or her own sin
Body, soul and spirit: the spirit is the part made to meet God, cut off at the fall and made alive again in Christ
The seventh day still kept: the Sabbath commandment stands for the people of God, and the day God blessed at creation is the day to keep
The Sabbath fulfilled in Christ's rest: the weekly day pointed ahead, and the rest it pointed to is found in Christ and shared by those who believe
The Lord's Day as the Christian Sabbath: the commandment stands, and the day of rest and worship now falls on the first day, the day of the resurrection
The gifts continue: speaking in tongues is a gift the Spirit still gives, for prayer and for the church
The sign gifts have ended (what is called cessationism): tongues belonged to the apostles' age, as a sign
The Spirit may give the gift today, and whatever is practiced is tested, interpreted and ordered
Wounded and healed: the fall brought death and disorder to every person, the image of God remains, and grace heals the will and moves it
Sin reaches every part of the person (what is called total depravity): left to itself no one seeks God or can turn to him, and God's grace gives the new heart
Grace that goes before (what is called prevenient grace): sin has left no one able to turn to God unaided, and God's grace given to everyone makes a free response possible
